title: Cinematic language and style
description:
## Background
Shot selection, movement, composition, background, perspective, mood and one consistent style per film (human notes, round 1).

## Success Criteria
All child beads closed; boards show the cinematic choices and the style profile.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 3), section 7a.

title: Define style profiles and four example profiles
description:
## Background
A film must be stylistically consistent: one look bounds every shot choice.

## Task
Add the style profile record (framing, angle and lens habits, movement, tonal key and contrast, light, palette, texture, editing rhythm, image aspect ratio) and four example profiles described by traits: symmetrical tableau, colour-field epic, Hong Kong police thriller, black-and-white noir. Each lists preferred and avoided values.

## Acceptance criteria
Profiles validate; each renders a three-shot sample sequence whose boards are recognisably different in framing, movement and key.

## Tests
Schema fixtures; human review of the four sample sequences.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 3), section 7a.6.

## Update (draft 4)
Round 2: approval 1 pins a style reference strip (wide, close, insert) by hash; shots inherit choices from profile then setup then overrides, with one reason per shot and reasons for departures. For generated films the first approved plate is pinned for palette and texture.

title: Support authored diagram and annotated-detail inserts as boards
description:
## Background
Some beats are explained more cheaply by a diagram than by a staged scene.

## Task
A shot may supply an authored diagram or annotated detail (SVG) directly as its board and final still, with source digest, evidence, style profile and must-see test, going through the same animatic and approval. Start with a side-on camera, hand and occluding body diagram for the pilot topic.

## Acceptance criteria
The pilot diagram plays in the animatic and passes the phone review protocol.

## Tests
Schema fixture; render check.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 4), sections 4 and 10.

title: Character sheets: turn posed mannequins into sketched characters
description:
## Background
Viewers follow people, not mannequins. A character sheet turns a posed mannequin into a recognisable sketched character, the same in every shot (human note, 2026-11-24).

## Task
Add the character sheet record (identity, body profile, silhouette shapes, garments as forms, value per garment, signature props, face option) and render a character layer on the posed figure: hairstyle, facial features, fingers, headwear as a simple solid, coats, sleeves and skirts as lofts on the body's own forms so they move with the pose, garment values feeding the value pass. Render a turnaround (front, three-quarter, side, back, one action pose) per character. The mannequin keeps its conventions (no fingers, no spiky hair, no hatching, clothed form); the character layer adds fingers posed from the three hand types, the character's real hairstyle (spiky included), facial features and hatching per the style profile, drawn the same way in every shot.

## Acceptance criteria
- Two characters in one frame are told apart at thumbnail size by a fresh viewer.
- A coat hangs and moves correctly with the pose in front, side and back views.
- Fingers, hair, features and hatching are identical in style across all turnaround views and every shot.
- Figures without a sheet render exactly as today (goldens unchanged).

## Tests
Golden turnarounds; schema fixtures.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 5), section 7b and roadmap row 6b.

## Update (draft 6)
Code draws silhouette, clothing and hair shape. Fingers and faces wait for the hands-and-faces spike decision.

title: Export boards as cutout layers by depth
description:
## Background
Phase A and B movement is parallax, which needs each board split into depth layers.

## Task
Render each board as separate transparent SVG/PNG layers: background (drawn complete, including what figures and props hide), midground set, each figure, foreground props, plus a JSON manifest of layer order and depth from the scene record. The flattened layers must equal the normal board.

## Acceptance criteria
Stacking the layers reproduces the board exactly; the background has no holes where cutouts sat.

## Tests
Flatten-and-compare test on the child-peek and balcony scenes.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 6), section 7a.3 and roadmap 3b.

title: Try code-drawn hands and faces, then decide
description:
## Background
Code-drawn fingers and faces tend to look stiff; the human decides after seeing attempts.

## Task
Draw fingers (posed from the open, fist and V hand types) and simple faces in the character layer for one character sheet: the turnaround plus three or four story poses. Present them side by side for a decision: keep code, or redraw hands and faces with an image model over the board.

## Acceptance criteria
The human records the decision on this bead and in the plan.

## Tests
None; this is a decision spike.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 6), section 7b.

title: Draw a light-versus-dark value pass on boards
description:
## Background
Line art alone cannot show mood; light versus dark is the main mood control.

## Task
A two- or three-tone shadow block-in (flat greys over paper) driven by tonal key and light motivation, in the sketch style. High-key mostly paper, low-key mostly dark with the subject picked out, silhouette as a flat dark shape.

## Acceptance criteria
High-key, low-key and silhouette versions of one scene read as different moods at phone size; the figure stays readable.

## Tests
Golden renders; v1 goldens unchanged when no key is set.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 3), sections 7a.3 and 8 row 3a.

title: Add keyframed 3D camera paths (after phase B)
description:
## Background
Movement (dolly, pan, tilt, crane, push-in) is a shot choice and must be judged in time.

## Task
Scene v2 optional camera path: keyframes of position, look-at and field of view over frames, with easing. Draw start and end boards with movement arrows; render in-between frames for the animatic; export the path as the motion instruction and as the push-in on held stills.

## Acceptance criteria
A dolly-in and a zoom from the same start frame visibly differ in perspective; the animatic plays the move.

## Tests
Path interpolation tests; golden start and end boards.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 3), sections 7a.3 and 8 row 3b.

## Update (draft 4)
Round 2: record the visible result each move must produce. A held still allows only a previewed crop inside its bounds; a reveal behind a foreground object needs a rendered path, a verified moving take, or a second board. Check the reveal frame and play the move for flicker.

## Update (draft 5)
Scope (draft 5): the storyboard film uses static shots; camera moves wait until a story needs them.

title: Composition overlay and framing checks
description:
## Background
Framing should be reviewable and partly checkable.

## Task
Optional overlay of thirds grid, safe area and caption band; checks for subject placement against the shot's composition, headroom and lead room, and tonal contrast of the subject against its background.

## Acceptance criteria
A subject placed on a third by a fixed camera lands within tolerance; missing lead room is flagged.

## Tests
Unit tests on projected bounds.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 3), sections 7a.3 and 8 row 3c.

title: Check cutting grammar across adjacent shots
description:
## Background
Shots are chosen as a sequence; some grammar can be checked from scene records.

## Task
Flag a crossed 180-degree line, a screen-direction or eyeline mismatch, and a size jump too small to read as intentional, between adjacent shots.

## Acceptance criteria
Each rule has a passing and a failing fixture pair.

## Tests
Fixture pairs.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 3), section 7a.2.

## Update (draft 4)
Round 2: read the continuity record (axis id if established, camera side, direction, who looks at what, subject side, size). Axis rules only where an axis is declared; deliberate breaks must be stated; ambiguous axes are left unscored. Project look directions for shot and reverse shot.

title: Flag shots that drift from the film's style profile
description:
## Background
Consistency needs checking, not just intent.

## Task
Compare each shot's cinematic fields with the style profile and flag avoided values or unexplained breaks (a handheld shot in a locked-off film, a high-key shot in a noir).

## Acceptance criteria
Flags appear on the review sheet; a break with a stated reason is shown but not flagged as an error.

## Tests
Fixtures per example profile.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 3), section 7a.6.

title: Build a library of named shot recipes
description:
## Background
The shot step needs starting points the way the figure has reference poses.

## Task
Scene records, boards and usage notes for: establishing wide to insert, over-the-shoulder pair, one-point perspective corridor, low-angle hero, high-angle isolation, silhouette against a window, dolly-in to a realisation, dolly zoom.

## Acceptance criteria
Each recipe renders and is reviewed by the human.

## Tests
Golden renders.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 3), section 7a.5.

title: Emphasise the focal subject and story detail; optional perspective guides
description:
## Background
The subject must read first and perspective must be visible.

## Task
Environments at lower line weight and detail than figures; faint horizon line and vanishing points from the camera; horizon placement treated as a composition choice.

## Acceptance criteria
In a street preset, a fresh viewer finds the figure first.

## Tests
Golden renders.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 3), section 8 row 6a.

## Update (draft 4)
Round 2: changed from "backgrounds lighter" to emphasis by focal subject and story detail: the story-bearing set detail (the rail in the peeking shot) keeps contrast, competing detail is subdued; perspective guides only on request, never on final boards.

title: Choose the first films' visual style: sketch or generated, and which style profile
description:
## Background
Open decision raised in round 1.

## Task
The human decides. Record the decision as a comment here and in the plan, then close it.

## Acceptance criteria
Decision recorded in both places.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 3), section 13 (Q7).

title: Assembly (stage 5)
description:
## Background
Groups the beads for plan section 5.5.

## Success Criteria
All child beads closed.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md, section 5.5.

title: Grow the rough-cut compiler into full assembly
description:
## Background
Phase B needs captions, music, motion clips and loudness control.

## Task
Extend the compiler: stills and clips, optional push-in on stills, crossfades, captions burned or sidecar, music mix, -16 LUFS integrated and peak at or below -1 dBTP, delivery size from the brief.

## Acceptance criteria
Correct size, fps and frame count; duration within one frame; cuts on cue frames.

## Tests
Stub media render with decode checks around cuts.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 2), section 6.

## Update (draft 4)
Round 2: same media-digest and anchor rules as the rough cut. Swapping only the selected take keeps board approval and reopens final approval; both phase B cuts reproduce offline.

title: Pipeline runner with stage receipts and approval checkpoints
description:
## Background
Stages exist separately; nothing runs them in order or knows what is stale.

## Task
`node bin/movie.js run <project>`: hash inputs, code and tool versions per stage; rebuild only stale outputs; write atomically; stop at script, animatic and final-cut approvals, which pin hashes.

## Acceptance criteria
Second run does no work; changing one shot rebuilds only that shot and the assembly; a changed title rebuilds only the release.

## Tests
End-to-end on the example project with stub services; interrupted writes; two concurrent runs.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 2), section 5.3.

title: Cut the approved boards to the narration as an animatic
description:
## Background
Voice before visuals: the storyboard is approved as a timed film before money is spent.

## Task
Use the rough-cut compiler to hold each board for its shot's span from word timings, with captions.

## Acceptance criteria
Producer approves the sequence; the approval pins every board hash.

## Tests
Recut after one changed line reuses unaffected shots.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 2), sections 2 and 4.

title: Frame the same scenes for portrait and landscape
description:
## Background
Landscape explainers come later; reuse scene records.

## Task
Per-delivery camera framing rules so one scene record yields both shapes, composed rather than letterboxed.

## Acceptance criteria
Both masters look intentionally composed.

## Tests
Visual check of both from one record.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 2), section 3, Q4.

title: Animate parallax drifts and push-ins from cutout layers in assembly
description:
## Background
Static boards risk feeling like a slideshow; parallax gives depth at almost no cost.

## Task
In the compiler, a shot may carry a parallax move (drift direction, push-in amount, duration, easing). Each layer is translated and scaled at a rate set by its depth, near layers more than far. Moves are capped so no cutout edge or frame edge shows.

## Acceptance criteria
A drift on the balcony scene shows the rail moving faster than the background, with no gaps or edges.

## Tests
Frame checks at start, middle and end; edge-exposure check.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 6), section 7a.3.

title: Storyboard (stage 2)
description:
## Background
Groups the beads for plan section 5.2.

## Success Criteria
All child beads closed.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md, section 5.2.

title: Joint limits on reach targets, named contact sites, structured diagnostics
description:
## Background
Reach targets bypass joint limits; warnings are plain strings; ladder rungs have no names.

## Task
Guard ik2 against zero distance and a pole parallel to the limb; compute achieved angles after solving and check them against the limits; name contact sites (rungs, rails) from the prop expansion; emit diagnostics with figure, joint, requested and achieved values and units, keeping today's strings.

## Acceptance criteria
A reachable target with an impossible elbow is reported; moving a rung moves its contact sites.

## Tests
Coincident targets, unreachable and too-close limbs, invalid spacing.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 2), section 8, order 4.

## Update (draft 3)
Round 1 (C4): diagnostics carry codes (target-outside-workspace, joint-range-exceeded, pole-conflict, contact-distance, prop-intersection, gaze-shortfall) plus a suggested fix. stand plus reach targets is invalid, not repairable. Section 7 step 5.

title: Annotate the reference poses by action, support and contacts
description:
## Background
Retrieval should match what touches what before matching words.

## Task
Add to each resource/pose record (or a sidecar index): action, support (floor, seat, rail, rung, airborne), contacts, camera sector, dynamic or static, allowed flexibility.

## Acceptance criteria
Requests for crouching, sitting and peeking, worded differently, retrieve the right starting records.

## Tests
Retrieval tests with paraphrased requests.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 2), section 7, step 2.

## Update (draft 3)
Round 1 (C1): annotations become validated pose-example records (setup id, support, contacts [{figure, joint, target}], gaze target, airborne, occlusion notes, scene hash). Two views of one setup share a setup id but stay separate results. Retrieval must show the requested contacts exist.

title: Build an evaluation set of 30 to 50 shot descriptions
description:
## Background
Description-to-scene needs a measurable benchmark.

## Task
Write varied shot descriptions with human-accepted scene records, covering every support type and camera sector.

## Acceptance criteria
Set committed; accept rate can be computed automatically.

## Tests
Every record validates and renders cleanly.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 2), section 7.

## Update (draft 3)
Round 1 (G4): keep the evaluation set apart from the retrieval library. Split by setup or brief family; withhold descriptions, solutions and notes from retrieval and tuning; replace any case that enters the library. Report first-pass accepts, accepts after repair, manual blocks, abandoned shots and minutes.

title: Generate a review sheet showing shots in sequence
description:
## Background
Storyboards are judged in sequence, not frame by frame.

## Task
HTML or PNG sheet: each frame at delivery size between its neighbours, with the shot's intent and must-see list; approval writes the frame hash into the shot record.

## Acceptance criteria
Changing a scene after approval marks the approval stale.

## Tests
Stale-approval test.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 2), sections 2, 4 and 7.

## Update (draft 3)
Human notes: add the thirds grid, safe area and caption band as an optional overlay, and show flags from the composition, continuity and style-drift checks beside each frame.

## Update (draft 4)
Round 2: follow the phone review protocol (delivery crop, fixed size, real caption band, fixed distance and duration, sound stated); show the style reference strip; play replacement plates between neighbours to catch mixed-media seams.

title: Write the cinematic heuristics guide
description:
## Background
The scene step needs explicit rules for camera height, lens feel and placement.

## Task
Short guide translating common shot words (low angle, over the shoulder, insert, reverse) into camera and framing rules used by the scene step.

## Acceptance criteria
A new contributor can predict the camera the scene step will choose.

## Tests
None.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 2), section 7.

## Update (draft 3)
Human notes: this guide becomes the mapping from the shot vocabulary (section 7a.1) to camera numbers: size and lens to distance and field of view, angle to height and pitch, composition to subject placement. It feeds desc2scene and the text route.

title: Solve gaze after grounding and measure the final gaze ray
description:
## Background
fig() aims the head at the look target before draw() moves the figure onto the floor, so a grounded figure can look past a nearby object with no warning.

## Task
For scene v2, finish support placement before solving gaze; report the angle between the final head-forward vector and the vector from the final eye point to the target, undefined for coincident points. Keep v1 drawings unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria
Two grounded figures of different heights looking at a nearby parcel report errors matching an independent measurement from exported transforms, including impossible turns.

## Tests
The fixture above; v1 goldens unchanged.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 4), section 5.2.

title: Warn when limbs pass through the body, each other or props
description:
## Background
A pose can be legal in numbers and wrong on paper.

## Task
Capsules for limb segments and torso parts, boxes and bars for props; report overlaps beyond a tolerance, excluding intended contacts.

## Acceptance criteria
Hands on a rail and sitting on a box do not warn; a forearm through the chest does.

## Tests
Unit tests for both.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 2), section 7, step 6.

title: Move renderer state into a per-render context, then split modules
description:
## Background
mannequin.js keeps mutable globals (P, GS, HS, BL, EX, FACE, CLAMPS, rnd), so render order can change output and multiple figures are unsafe.

## Task
First move all mutable state into a context created per render. Then split into math, shapes, skeleton, render and api modules with readable names. No behaviour change.

## Acceptance criteria
Golden tests pass byte for byte; frames rendered in any order match; public API unchanged.

## Tests
Golden tests plus an order-shuffling test.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 2), section 8, order 2.

title: Add environment presets: ground, rooms, cuboid buildings, doors, windows
description:
## Background
Frames show figures and a few props, with no place.

## Task
Named presets that expand into geometry (room with visible or cutaway walls, street kerb and facade, ground plane), drawn in the sketch style and depth-sorted with figures.

## Acceptance criteria
Interior and street reference scenes added and reviewed by the human; a reverse angle keeps the door.

## Tests
Golden renders; schema updated.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 2), section 8, order 7.

title: Add a key light and cast shadows
description:
## Background
Chui cares about light in rooms and exteriors at dawn, evening and night with headlights and wet ground.

## Task
Start with one directional light and planar floor shadows. Later: point lights, headlights, reflections on wet ground.

## Acceptance criteria
Two angles of one set show consistent light; monochrome still readable at phone size.

## Tests
Golden renders; v1 goldens unchanged.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 2), section 8, order 7.

## Update (draft 3)
Human notes: lighting is driven by the shot's tonal key and light motivation (section 7a): high-key, low-key, silhouette; window, lamp, sun at dawn, golden hour, blue hour and night, headlights. The two- or three-tone value pass is a separate, earlier bead.

title: Draw several figures in one frame with namespaced joints
description:
## Background
Shots often need two people; the renderer assumes one.

## Task
Scene v2 `figures` array; one depth-sorted draw list across figures; joint and part names namespaced so one torso cannot hide the other figure's arm by tag collision; props anchored to a named figure's joints.

## Acceptance criteria
Two people share a floor at correct relative size and overlap; a box held by one figure.

## Tests
Golden renders; circular anchor rejected.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 2), section 8, order 6.

title: Turn a shot description into a scene record with bounded repair
description:
## Background
Every scene record so far was hand-written.

## Task
Implement section 7: parse intent, retrieve by contact topology, resolve named anchors, try bounded camera candidates, render, apply allow-listed fixes for at most two rounds, never raise flexibility to clear warnings, and hand impossible requests to manual blocking.

## Acceptance criteria
On the evaluation set, at least 80% produce valid records passing automatic checks within two rounds; the human reviews a sample.

## Tests
Automated on the evaluation set.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 2), section 7.

## Update (draft 3)
Human notes: map the shot's cinematic fields to camera numbers via the heuristics mapping, inside the style profile; candidate framings must respect the profile.

title: Add a fixed camera mode beside automatic framing
description:
## Background
draw() always rescales and centres on the figure, so a camera cannot stay put across shots or place a subject on a third.

## Task
Camera `mode: "fixed"` with position, look-at, vertical field of view, roll and frame width and height; near-plane clipping; a usable up vector when looking straight down. Keep `"fit"` as the default for v1.

## Acceptance criteria
- A figure moved across a fixed frame changes position and size.
- Portrait and landscape render without stretching.
- v1 goldens unchanged.

## Tests
Centre-to-edge translation, distance scaling, vertical camera, near-plane crossing.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 2), section 8, order 3.

## Update (draft 3)
Round 1 (G5): build on the fixed scale-and-offset path draw() already uses for renderLineup (sh.fix). Acceptance: a locked camera keeps a world marker on the same pixel as the subject moves; near-plane crossings are clipped, never projected from behind the lens.

title: Export contour, skeleton, depth and object-id layers
description:
## Background
Generation routes and visibility checks need machine-readable layers from the same camera.

## Task
From one projection, write a clean contour image (no frame border, no construction), a joint skeleton image, a depth image and an object-id image where each surface has a flat colour, plus projected joint positions in normalised screen coordinates.

## Acceptance criteria
In both ladder views, overlays line up with the sketch; the boot-over-rung overlap matches the object-id pass.

## Tests
Golden images; visibility of hand-labelled points.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 2), section 8, order 5.

## Update (draft 3)
Round 1 (G5): keep stable part and prop ids through geometry expansion, and add a visibility check for occlusion-critical regions that compares camera-space depth along shared rays with simple surface proxies. The current single average-depth sort can paint a wrong overlap. Acceptance: a crossing-bars fixture switches visible id at the known crossing; disagreements are flagged, never auto-accepted.

## Update (draft 5)
Scope (draft 5): only the visibility check is needed for the storyboard film; the generation exports (contour, skeleton, depth) are deferred with generation.

title: Data contracts and project folder
description:
## Background
Groups the beads for plan section 4.

## Success Criteria
All child beads closed.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md, section 4.

title: Write versioned schemas for production records and scene v2
description:
## Background
Stages communicate only through files; formats are prose today.

## Task
Add the record envelope and JSON Schemas under `schema/` for brief, beat, shot, scene (v1 and v2), board receipt, attempt, voice, captions, mix, edit and release. Scene v2: camera mode fit or fixed, environment, lights, figures array with namespaced joints, required `look`. Shot: mustSee, mayHide, inCue, cutFrom.

## Acceptance criteria
- All 18 resource/pose records validate as v1.
- The section 5.2 example validates as v2.
- Unknown keys, wrong array lengths and missing `look` in v2 fail with a path.

## Tests
Positive and negative fixtures per schema.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 2), section 5.1 and 5.2.

## Update (draft 3)
Round 1 and human notes: scenes use the common envelope (kind "scene", version 1 or 2, payload), no sceneVersion field; the CLI still accepts bare v1 files. Add records: pose example, labour, style profile. Shot gains cueOffsetFrames and the cinematic fields (size, angle, lens, composition, layers, move, key, motivation, reason). Brief gains a style profile id. Edit becomes interval list. Sections 5.1, 5.2, 7a.

## Update (draft 4)
Round 2: add records asset provenance, motion, continuity and style reference (section 5.1). Edit intervals gain `media` (kind and digest of the exact drawing, still or clip) and `anchor` (speech cue plus offset, or picture beat plus frame). Beat records gain target duration and minimum screen time.

## Update (draft 5)
Scope (draft 5): add the story and screenplay-scene records; beats gain what happens, intended effect, characters, and speaker for dialogue.

title: Validate scene records in the pose CLI before rendering
description:
## Background
Bad records currently render something odd instead of failing.

## Task
Add a dependency-free validator and a `node lib/pose/cli.js validate <file|folder>` command. `render` validates first and exits non-zero with a readable message on failure.

## Acceptance criteria
- Invalid record: non-zero exit, and the message names the field.
- Valid records render as before (golden tests unchanged).

## Tests
CLI tests for valid and invalid input.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md, section 4.

title: Define projects/ and runs/ folders with the pilot as the example
description:
## Background
Inputs and large outputs need separate homes.

## Task
`projects/<slug>/` holds small committed inputs; `runs/<slug>/` holds frames, audio, plates, masters, cost ledger and run log, ignored by git. Make `projects/pilot/` the example and document the layout.

## Acceptance criteria
The pilot project validates and its scenes render into runs/pilot/.

## Tests
Test that renders the example project from scratch.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 2), section 5.

title: Reserve and reconcile spend per film
description:
## Background
Paid calls must never exceed the per-film cap, even after a crash.

## Task
Per-film USD ledger in runs/: persist intent and reserved maximum before each network call, the provider job id right after, and settle on confirmation. Unknown charges stay counted at their maximum.

## Acceptance criteria
Two competing requests with money for one: the second is refused. A crash after submission resumes by polling.

## Tests
Fake provider that completes late, fails after submission, or loses the response.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 2), sections 5.3 and 9.

## Update (draft 3)
Round 1 (G3): serialise reservation decisions per film under one lock shared by all workers and reruns; check settled plus outstanding maximums plus the new maximum against the cap. A submission that may have succeeded without a recorded job id keeps its reservation open and is marked unresolved until billing or job evidence settles it. Test a lost acknowledgement plus restart, and two workers competing for the last funds. See section 5.3.

## Update (draft 5)
Scope (draft 5): paid generation is deferred; the ledger is needed only once a paid voice or generation service is used.

title: Record producer labour per task
description:
## Background
Labour is the real cost and a phase C exit criterion, but nothing records it.

## Task
Producer-entered labour records (stage, task, start and end, active seconds, blocker type, notes) and a report of median and maximum minutes by stage, plus manual-blocking count.

## Acceptance criteria
A film's report totals active minutes from brief to private master, including rejected takes.

## Tests
Report generated from a fixture ledger.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 3), sections 5.1 and 11.

title: Run the blind generation route experiment
description:
## Background
The main risk is that models ignore the board.

## Task
Section 10: eight intents x three routes (text, reference, structural control) x two attempts, labels hidden, two reviewers, minutes logged. Pay from development, not a film.

## Acceptance criteria
A written decision per shot class using the pre-set 20-point rule, approved by the human.

## Tests
Scoring sheet checked with a deliberately wrong-rung image first.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 2), section 10.

## Update (draft 3)
Redesigned (round 1, G1): compare whole workflows first (direct prompt written from the brief vs blocking the scene and sending the board plus a scene-derived prompt), timed from brief to approval. Isolate the picture only on disputed shots; structural control only on a demonstrated failure. Alternate views of one setup count once; the approved drawing is scored too. The producer sets the value of one extra usable shot before running (Q8); small or mixed results stay provisional. See section 10.

## Update (draft 4)
Round 2: on graphically answerable briefs, also cut a simple diagram or annotated insert into the slot and ask a fresh viewer the question; if it works within budget it stays eligible.

title: Build the still-generation adapter
description:
## Background

## Acceptance criteria

## Tests
Fake service: throttling, rejected input, expired links, lost submission response.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 2), sections 6 and 11.

## Update (draft 4)
Round 2: write a complete asset provenance record (source, model and settings, dated terms snapshot, inputs, public-use and disclosure flags) with every download; incomplete provenance makes an asset ineligible for the edit.

title: Animate one approved still

## Tests

## Update (draft 4)
Round 2: each motion take is checked against the shot's motion contract over the whole interval: locked contacts kept, forbidden changes absent. A good final frame is not enough.

title: Turn a story into a screenplay with intended beats
description:
## Background
Stage 1 does not exist.

## Task
Brief to beats: opening question, observable change, answer; 65 to 90 spoken words for 30 to 45 seconds; spoken and display text, cue IDs, evidence per claim.

## Acceptance criteria
Validates against the beat schema; narration length within 10% of target at the voice's rate.

## Tests
Schema and length checks.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 2), section 6.

## Update (draft 4)
Round 2: word budget comes from a test read or the chosen voice's measured rate (65 to 90 words is a first estimate only); each beat has a target duration and minimum screen time; at least a second of lead and resolution around each observable change.

## Update (draft 5)
Scope (draft 5): input is a story record (logline, premise, characters with body profiles, setting, turning change, length, style profile); output is scenes with location and time of day, broken into beats. Each beat states what happens, its intended effect on the audience, who is in it, and narration or dialogue with cue words. Approval 1 covers the story, the beats, pronunciation and the style profile. Depends on Q1 only for narration versus dialogue.

title: Turn approved beats into a shot list
description:
## Background
Storyboarding works per shot, and each shot must change what the viewer knows.

## Task

## Acceptance criteria
Every beat covered; adjacent screen direction checked.

## Tests
Schema validation.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 2), section 6.

## Update (draft 3)
Human notes: each shot chooses size, angle, lens, composition, depth layers, movement, tonal key and light motivation from the vocabulary, inside the film's style profile, with a reason; the sequence follows the grammar in section 7a.2.

## Update (draft 5)
Scope (draft 5): every shot traces to a screenplay beat and its intended effect.

title: Add golden regression tests for the reference renders
description:
## Background
lib/pose has no tests; every renderer change risks silently altering frames.

## Task
Add `test/pose.golden.test.js` (`node --test`). At seed 11 render every resource/pose scene, both construction modes, the sheet and the line-up; compare SVG text exactly with `test/golden/`. `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1` regenerates. Add a script that renders old, new and a difference image side by side for human approval of intended changes.

## Acceptance criteria
- `node --test` passes on a clean checkout.
- Changing one profile number fails and names the scenes.
- Render order does not affect results (fails today; fixed by the per-render-state bead).

## Tests
The test itself; determinism for a fixed seed.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 2), sections 8 (order 1) and 9.

## Update (draft 3)
Round 1 (C5): add a renderer manifest naming each fixture, seed, expected warning codes, and whether it is a frame, sheet or line-up case. A folder scan may discover files but does not decide coverage.
close_reason: Completed: test/pose.golden.test.js with manifest test/pose-manifest.json covers 18 scenes x 2 construction modes, sheet and 2 line-ups (39 goldens); determinism, render-order and can-fail tests; 45/45 pass; a one-attribute change to frame-dash golden fails exactly that test; test/golden-review.js writes old/new/difference page

title: Test the renderer warnings: clamped joints, unreachable targets, gaze shortfall
description:
## Background

## Task

## Acceptance criteria
Each warning type has a test asserting its text pattern.

## Tests
As described.

## Reference
lib/pose/README.md, "Use".

title: Produce the first storyboard film (phase B)
description:
## Background
The first product is a storyboard film: static boards with full cinematic intent, voice and a light music bed (human decision, 2026-11-24).

## Task
Write a short story (about 60 to 90 seconds), turn it into a screenplay with intended beats, choose a style profile, block each shot as a static board (two figures and simple environments where needed, value pass for mood), record the voice, cut the animatic, add a light music bed and captions, and assemble. Producer minutes recorded.

## Acceptance criteria
A fresh viewer retells the story's turn and names what the main character wanted; every shot traces to a beat; the film plays on a phone with captions.

## Tests
Phone review protocol; comprehension check.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 5), sections 1.1 and 11 (phase B).

title: Record the pilot narration and mark word onsets
description:
## Background

## Task
Record a human read (or one Polly request with speech marks if Q3 is already decided). Store the audio as 48 kHz mono WAV and a timings file with each word's onset in samples.

## Acceptance criteria
A clean 15 to 20 second read with a usable breath at the cut; the cue word onset is marked.

## Tests
Script, transcript and heard words agree.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 2), sections 4, 6 and 11.

## Update (draft 3)
Round 1 (G6): hand-mark caption phrase bounds and named cut cues on the actual take, stored as sample offsets with the audio hash, so a pickup cannot reuse stale marks.

## Update (draft 6)
Now for the child-peek micro-story (single narrator, human read).

title: Block and render the micro-story boards
description:
## Background

## Task
Block each shot as a scene record from the child-peek scene (new camera per shot), render at the delivery size, and export cutout layers for the one parallax shot.

## Acceptance criteria

## Tests

docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 6), sections 7a and 11.

title: Build the minimal compiler: stills, hard cuts and voice to MP4
description:
## Background
Nothing yet turns pictures and audio into a video.

## Task
Read a small edit record (integer frame timeline at 30 fps) and call FFmpeg with argument arrays: still images held for their spans, hard cuts, PCM voice, H.264 and AAC in MP4. Check the FFmpeg version and needed filters at startup.

## Acceptance criteria
A playable MP4 where the change of angle lands on the marked cue frame.

## Tests
Decode the frames either side of each cut; duration matches the audio sample count within one frame.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 2), sections 6 and 11.

## Update (draft 3)
Round 1 (C3, G6): the edit is a list of half-open integer frame intervals (startFrame, endFrame, shot, board hash, source range, transition); cut positions come from the voice hash plus each shot's cue and signed offset. Reject empty or reversed intervals. See section 5.1.

## Update (draft 4)
Round 2: intervals select media by digest and verify bytes before assembly; stills omit source bounds; anchors are speech (cue plus offset) or picture (beat plus frame) so a silent cut works.

title: Caption and package the pilot
description:
## Background

## Task
Group the marked words into phrases, write WebVTT, and package the clean master, captions, a cover frame, title and a rights list (all owned).

## Acceptance criteria

## Tests

docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 2), sections 6 and 11.

## Tests
